html:
The Mongol Empire was the largest contiguous land empire in history. Founded on the Mongolian steppe in 1206, it stretched at its height from Korea and the Sea of Japan to Hungary, and from Siberia to the Persian Gulf.

Genghis Khan united the steppe tribes and began the Mongol conquests. His sons and grandsons sent armies in every direction:

  • Under Ögedei (1229 to 1241): north China was conquered and the capital Karakorum built. Batu's armies took the Rus' cities and invaded Europe, reaching Poland and Hungary in 1241.
  • Under Möngke (1251 to 1259): Hülegü destroyed the Assassins and the sack of Baghdad in 1258 ended the Abbasid caliphate.
  • Under Kublai Khan (1260 to 1294): the conquest of Song China was completed in 1279.

The empire linked East and West. Under the Pax Mongolica, merchants, envoys, missionaries and craftsmen moved between China, Iran and Europe. Paper money, gunpowder and printing techniques travelled, and so, probably, did the plague that later became the Black Death.

The cost was immense. Cities that resisted were often destroyed and their people killed. Iran, Iraq and north China lost a large share of their population.

Unity did not last. After Möngke died in 1259, his brothers Kublai and Ariq Böke fought for the throne. By 1294, when Kublai died, the empire had become four successor states that often fought each other:

  • the Yuan dynasty in China and Mongolia
  • the Golden Horde on the western steppe
  • the Ilkhanate in Iran
  • the Chagatai Khanate in Central Asia
sum: The Mongol Empire was the largest contiguous land empire in history. Founded on the Mongolian steppe in 1206, it stretched at its height from Korea and the Sea of Japan to Hungary, and from Siberia to the Persian Gulf.
